turnaround_reason: Coty trades near $2.92 (52-week low $1.82) after years of soft Consumer Beauty trends, but is executing a credible deleveraging and cost-out story: net debt down ~$840M YoY to $2.9B, ~3.4x leverage targeting ~2x, with the 'Coty.Curated' reset underway.
bullish_points: Q4 like-for-like sales down only 1%, ahead of mid-single-digit-decline guidance, with better US prestige fragrance and mass cosmetics orders
Deleveraging is tangible: net debt -$840M YoY, FCF $348M (+~$70M YoY), 'All in to Win' delivered $250M+ savings ahead of target
Returning the Gucci Beauty license to Kering for ~$400M ($250M upfront) provides cash and simplifies the portfolio
Optically cheap equity where each turn of debt reduction is highly accretive to the thin equity stub
Prestige fragrance remains a resilient category
bearish_points: Heavy leverage remains the dominant risk: $3.3B total debt vs only $176M cash; EV $6.1B dwarfs the $2.6B cap
Management withheld full-year FY2027 guidance citing Coty.Curated implementation and strategic review — an uncertainty flag
Consumer Beauty demand is still soft and negative profit margin (-10%) shows the P&L isn't fixed yet
Barchart framing that the turnaround 'hinges on whether vendors keep waiting' hints at working-capital/supplier fragility
Dossier technicals null; low-priced stock with high sensitivity to any liquidity scare
catalyst: Continued net-debt reduction plus Coty.Curated execution stabilizing Consumer Beauty; the Gucci license cash inflow
suggested_trade: Small spot only; treat as a levered deleveraging option, size accordingly
key_risk: Consumer Beauty demand deteriorates and leverage forces dilutive or distressed action before the debt glide-path completes
would_skip_if: A guide-down on FCF/leverage, or evidence supplier terms are tightening
